assessment.title: Programming Fundamentals — Section-End Assessment
assessment.description: 12 MCQs. Passing threshold 70% is required alongside 8/10 lessons completed to unlock Arrays.

questions.text: The primary purpose of a variable in a program is to:
options: Store a value that can be referenced and possibly updated
questions.explanation: A variable is a named storage location holding a value that may be read or reassigned.

questions.text: What does the data type of a variable determine?
options: The kinds of values it can hold and the operations allowed on it
questions.explanation: The type constrains the value domain and which operations are defined.

questions.text: In most statically typed languages (C, Java, Go), what does `10 / 3` evaluate to when both operands are integers?
questions.explanation: Integer division truncates the fractional part.

Executes a block only if a condition is true
questions.explanation: if is a selection construct: the block runs only when the condition is truthy.

questions.text: The main difference between a `for` loop and a `while` loop is:
options: `for` loops are typically used when the number of iterations is known, while `while` loops repeat based on a condition
questions.explanation: Both are repetition constructs; the choice usually reflects whether iteration count is known in advance.

questions.text: What is the output of `x = 5; if x > 3: x = x + 2; print(x)`?
questions.explanation: 5 > 3 is true, so x becomes 5 + 2 = 7 and prints 7.

questions.text: What does `2 + 3 * 4` evaluate to in most languages?
questions.explanation: Multiplication has higher precedence than addition, so 3*4 = 12 is evaluated first.

questions.text: In the nested loop `for i in range(3): for j in range(4): print(i, j)`, how many times does the inner statement execute?
questions.explanation: The inner loop runs fully for each of the 3 outer iterations: 3 * 4 = 12.

questions.text: What is the difference between a parameter and an argument?
options: A parameter is the variable declared in the function's signature; an argument is the value passed at the call site
Arguments are only for functions that return values
Parameters are passed at call time; arguments are declared in the definition
questions.explanation: Parameters describe the function's interface; arguments are the concrete values bound to them.
Arrays are 0-indexed, so index 2 is the third element, 30.

questions.text: What is the output of `def f(a, b): return a - b` followed by `print(f(5, 3))`?
What is the time complexity of accessing the k-th element of an array of n elements?
questions.explanation: Array access is constant-time via address arithmetic, independent of k or n.
